STIFF-LIMB SYNDROME WITH IDENTIFICATION OF
GLUTAMIC ACID ANTIDECARBOXYLASE ANTIBODY
GAD65: A CASE REPORT.
Natalia Jaramillo (Bogotá, Colombia), Claudia Pena (Bogotá, Colombia)
INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND: Stiff-limb syndrome (SLS),
variant of Stiff-person syndrome, is characterized by longterm
progressive muscular rigidity and painful muscle spasms, in relation to
the existence of autoimmune disorders.
CASE REPORT: A 28-year-old male patient was referred for EDX
testing. He had a 2-month history of subacute weakness syndrome of
progressive and rapid establishment, with marked difficulty in muscle
relaxation, rigidity, spasms and cramp pain in the lower limbs,
functional limitation, and inability to walk. He also had a medical
history of type 1 diabetes mellitus, Graves’ disease, and anxiety disorder.
Laboratory study results showed positive microsomal antibodies and
high levels of creatine phosphokinase. Thyroid ultrasound reported a
diffuse goiter, with a hypervascular pattern and inflammatory nodes.
His cerebral and spine MRI were normal. NCSs showed normal motor
and sensory nerve action potentials. Needle EMG showed normal
insertional activity, normal recruitment in facial musculature and upper
limbs; in the lower limbs muscle relaxation was not achieved, and they
showed continuous motor unit activity. Considering SLS, glutamic acid
decarboxylase 65-kD isoform (GAD65) antibody testing was requested
and was found positive. Pharmacological management with a
antithyroid drug, diazepam, and baclofen is initiated, achieving
significant clinical improvement in spasm and pain modulation and gait
recovery.
SUMMARY/CONCLUSION: We present the first case of SLS in our
institution, a young man with subacute clinical manifestation. In our
country, it is a low frequency entity with higher presentation in women.
This report illustrates the utility of EDX studies along with
autoimmunity testing and clinical findings in the diagnosis of this
pathology.
Natalia Jaramillo, MD
Resident and Fellow Member Award Recipient
